# Journal compression — facts

> Source-anchored units about Journal compression: 16 across 6 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-31 · 16 units · 6 sources · rights: quote -->

## Definitions

- [statement] The WiredTiger journal is a write-ahead log used to recover changes after the last checkpoint; journal compression changes the representation of this recovery data. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/journaling.md · keywords: Journal compression · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/manage-journaling.md

## How it works

- [statement] MongoDB's standalone procedure changes journalCompressor, cleanly shuts down mongod, confirms the process has stopped, and restarts with the new configuration; --wiredTigerJournalCompressor is the command-line alternative. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/manage-journaling.md · keywords: Journal compression

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Use db.serverStatus().wiredTiger.log to monitor journal statistics when evaluating compressor changes. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/journaling.md · keywords: Journal compression · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/manage-journaling.md

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Mark Callaghan’s March 2014 insert benchmark reported roughly 10% more inserts per second for some configurations with journal compression disabled. The post tested MongoDB 2.6.0-rc0; this is historical evidence, not a measured WiredTiger or current-version improvement. (low confidence) — https://smalldatum.blogspot.com/2014/03/redo-logs-in-mongodb-and-innodb.html · keywords: Journal compression

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] SERVER-17251 reported an apparent throughput effect from journalCompressor even with journaling disabled on MongoDB 3.0.0-rc8, but MongoDB closed it as Cannot Reproduce; the issue does not establish a confirmed compressor performance regression. (low confidence) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-17251 · keywords: Journal compression
- [statement] MongoDB's journaling documentation states that WiredTiger does not compress log records of 128 bytes or less, its minimum log-record size; journal-compression savings therefore cannot be assumed for those records. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/journaling.md · keywords: Journal compression

## Facts and statements

- [statement] MongoDB 8.0 documents storage.wiredTiger.engineConfig.journalCompressor with default snappy and supported values none, snappy, zlib, and zstd; Dell's deployment guide shows the same journal-specific configuration. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.0/reference/configuration-options/ · keywords: Journal compression · also: https://infohub.delltechnologies.com/en-us/l/dell-powerstore-mongodb-solution-guide/wiredtiger-storage-engine-2/, https://infohub.delltechnologies.com/fr-fr/l/dell-powerstore-mongodb-solution-guide/wiredtiger-storage-engine-2/
- [statement] Journal compression and collection block compression are separate settings: engineConfig.journalCompressor controls journal data, while collectionConfig.blockCompressor controls collection blocks. Treating collection compression results as journal-specific savings would conflate these settings. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.0/reference/configuration-options/ · keywords: Journal compression · also: https://infohub.delltechnologies.com/en-us/l/dell-powerstore-mongodb-solution-guide/wiredtiger-storage-engine-2/, https://infohub.delltechnologies.com/fr-fr/l/dell-powerstore-mongodb-solution-guide/wiredtiger-storage-engine-2/
- [statement] WiredTiger does not compress journal records whose size is less than or equal to 128 bytes. The implementation README also describes a small-record exception, but leaves its threshold uncertain. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/journaling.md · keywords: Journal compression · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/storage/wiredtiger/README.md
- [statement] Google's Snappy documentation describes a design that favors high speed and reasonable compression over maximum compression. Its compression ratios vary substantially with the input; these algorithm benchmarks are not measurements of MongoDB journal savings. (low confidence) — https://github.com/google/snappy · keywords: Journal compression
- [statement] Inference: for compressible journal records, compression can reduce journal bytes and file turnover relative to none. Actual benefit depends on record size and compressibility, so a fixed journal cost-reduction percentage is unsupported. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/journaling.md · keywords: Journal compression · also: https://github.com/google/snappy, https://dba.stackexchange.com/questions/171324/change-journalcompressor-to-none-not-default-snappy
- [statement] If mongod shuts down uncleanly during a journal-compressor change, MongoDB instructs operators to recover using the old compressor settings before retrying the change. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/manage-journaling.md · keywords: Journal compression
- [statement] Journal files are preallocated; WiredTiger removes old files while retaining those needed for recovery from the last checkpoint. Therefore compression ratio alone is insufficient to size the journal directory. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/journaling.md · keywords: Journal compression
- [statement] Selecting journalCompressor=none disables compression of journal data. It does not disable journaling: MongoDB's journaling documentation states that journaling is always enabled starting in 6.1 and storage.journal.enabled was removed. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v8.0/reference/configuration-options/ · keywords: Journal compression · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/journaling.md
- [statement] db.serverStatus() exposes journal statistics in wiredTiger.log. The journaling documentation describes this field as information about the WiredTiger journal; it does not present a universal compression-savings percentage. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/journaling.md · keywords: Journal compression · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/manage-journaling.md, https://github.com/google/snappy
- [statement] WiredTiger removes journal files no longer needed for recovery from the last checkpoint. MongoDB warns that disabling compression changes journal-space calculations and that insufficient journal disk space can crash the server, so journal compression does not justify eliminating recovery headroom. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/journaling.md · keywords: Journal compression
